title: Before Executor Agents launch, an Executor Agent is a GovOps actor and a Facilitator acting jointly
content:
A.1.14.4.7.1 defines a substitution rather than a suspension: "In the short term, before the launch of Executor Agents, all references to Executor Agents in the Atlas refer to a GovOps Actor and a Facilitator, collectively. Sky Governance designates these actors as an Executor Agent on a transitional basis, and they have all the powers of Executor Agents as defined in the Atlas." Crucially, entering an Accord in this period "requires the mutual agreement of both the GovOps actor and the Facilitator, in addition to the Prime Agent."

The design choice is that the Atlas's Executor provisions are written against a *role*, so the role can be filled by existing actors without amending any of the surrounding text. Nothing about Executor duties, refusal rights or unamendable alignment checks has to be restated for the transition.

Requiring both parties to consent turns the transitional Executor into a two-of-two rather than a merged entity. That deliberately preserves the internal separation A.1.14.4.6.1.2 depends on — if GovOps alone could bind the pair, the Facilitator's reserved interpretation and key-holding role would be subordinated at the moment of contracting.

A.1.14.4.7.2 and A.1.14.4.7.3 describe the path onward: limited Executor Agents launch shortly after Prime Agents, all Sky Core budgets transfer out to Agents, and during that phase "GovOps controlling the budget of the Executor Agent subject to review for alignment by the Facilitator" — the same two-role check applied to money. Eventually Executors launch "with their own tokens and governance processes," at which point "GovOps actors and Facilitators will be contracted by Executor Agents through a vote of Executor Agent token holders," inverting the relationship: the actors that currently *constitute* the Executor become its employees.
description: The pair holds all Executor powers transitionally, and an Executor Accord in this period needs the agreement of both plus the Prime Agent — preserving the internal split as a two-of-two.
